The tax cost of selling would be substantial, requiring a very high hurdle to justify liquidation [D04].

final.memo:
We regard Apple as a wonderful business that maintains a significant competitive advantage through its consumer-device and services ecosystem [D01]. The latest quarterly results show a resilient business, with record services revenue offsetting temporary hardware weakness [D03]. We do not sell businesses of this quality simply because Mr. Market is enthusiastic or because we face short-term revenue fluctuations [D04, D05].

Our holding period is indefinite, and we remain satisfied with the underlying economics of the business [D01, D07]. Apple's ability to drive repeat purchases and recurring software spending provides a durable moat that protects its pricing power [D01]. Management continues to allocate capital rationally, demonstrated by the recent dividend increase and significant share repurchase authorization [D02].

We must remain mindful of our substantial tax cost in the event of a sale [D04, D08]. With a 21% federal corporate tax rate, a sale must clear a high after-tax hurdle, and we see no reason to trigger such a cost when the business thesis remains intact [D04]. We hold our position, confident in the company's long-term prospects as an integral part of our equity portfolio [D08].
